title: LOLBins/LOLBAS
overview: Triage a signed Windows binary invoked by an unusual parent and directed at an untrusted content location.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A signed proxy binary launched by an office parent with user-writable content warrants process-chain review.
evidence: Inspect parent, path provenance and signer. Review any related child process and connection events.
false_positive: A legacy business application can invoke these Windows binaries from Office automation.
tuning: Constrain an exception to an approved process chain and module path, with review when either changes.
response: Preserve lineage and metadata. Scope unintended effects before isolating the endpoint.
prevention: Use application control and audit document applications that launch child processes.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The record contains process names and context only. It provides no executable arguments.

questions.prompt: Why does the signed executable still deserve review?
options: Its parent and content provenance are unusual
A signature means it is always unauthorized
questions.explanation: Context distinguishes trustworthy software from unsafe use of it.

options: An exception for all signed binaries
Visibility of unapproved parent and content combinations
questions.explanation: Broad trust loses the relationship the rule relies on.
